correctness.rationale: On an arbitrary equilateral set M=Gamma x N x signs, T is isometric because both extrema are approached through r_k->1. Every nonzero image has strict pointwise gap; the zero-sum ell1 model of F(M) proves nonattainment as a predual functional by positivity of mass at strict interior values. Coordinate extraction at level one gives weak-star closed range via pointwise linear identities. The level-k extraction and its molecule witnesses give w-star continuous projections with exact norm 1/r_k; their infimum is one. A w-star continuous norm-one projection would compose with a coefficient functional to create a norm-one predual functional attained at T(e_gamma), contradiction. Hahn--Banach limit extension gives a bounded norm-one projection, necessarily not w-star continuous. No finite computation substitutes for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The mathematically motivated invariant is the best projection norm under preservation of the canonical Lipschitz-free weak-star structure. In a natural infinite equilateral model, its exact infimum exists but is not attained, despite ordinary projection norm one being attained by injectivity. The explicit sharp approximating family and nonattainment obstruction distinguish predual-compatible complementability from ordinary Banach complementability, a structural boundary not provided by mere spaceability or a routine scalar classification.
